summary: Iteration 10: SECURITY HARDENING full validation. Added /app/backend/tests/test_security.py (37 new tests). Full pytest 86/86 pass in 34s. All hardening features validated: JWT token versioning (old token 401 after change-pin), progressive lockout (5 wrong PINs -> 429 with 'min' message, count persists in db.login_attempts), security headers (X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cache-Control no-store on /api), document upload sanitization (../..<script>evil</script>.txt -> stripped bad chars, client content_type ignored, txt served as attachment with text/plain), .exe/.html/.svg rejected 400, all 14 protected endpoints return 401 for no-token AND garbage-token, CORS echoes allowed origin & withholds ACAO for evil origin (verified against localhost:8001 — see note below). Frontend regression: PIN 1234 unlock, all 3 tabs load with correct seed counts (2 creds, 1 card, 1 ins), add+delete credential works, Change PIN 1234->5678 succeeds WITHOUT re-locking UI (silent re-unlock via ChangePinDialog effect), continued browsing on Cards tab worked, revert 5678->1234 also without re-lock. Final state: PIN=1234, db.login_attempts empty, seed intact.
critical_code_review_comments: Progressive lockout math is sound: cycles = count // 5, lock_min = 15 * 2^(cycles-1), capped 1440 (24h). Counter is NOT reset on lockout expiry — only on successful unlock — which is exactly the requested 'persist across windows' behavior.
require_auth compares int(payload.ver) == int(vault.token_ver). Since $inc default and payload defaults are both 0-safe, this correctly invalidates ALL prior tokens the moment change-pin runs.
safe_filename regex `[^A-Za-z0-9._ -]` correctly strips <, >, path separators, control chars. The Path(...).name call defeats '../..' traversal at the OS level. 100-char cap prevents FS abuse. Good.

download_document derives media_type ONLY from ext (whitelist lookup with octet-stream fallback) and forces attachment disposition for non-inline types. This kills stored-XSS via forged content_type — verified: uploaded a txt with client-declared content_type='text/html', downloaded as text/plain attachment.

CORS: FastAPI CORSMiddleware correctly echoes ALLOWED_ORIGIN and withholds ACAO for evil origin (verified via curl on localhost:8001). NOTE: The public preview URL sits behind Cloudflare edge which overwrites ACAO to '*' on OPTIONS regardless — this is the preview infra, NOT the app. User's own nginx (per request note) does not do this, so production behavior is correct. CORS tests point at localhost:8001 for this reason.
Security headers middleware runs AFTER call_next, so 401/400/500 responses ALSO get the headers — verified.

One subtle observation (not a bug, worth noting): the lockout gate `attempt.count >= MAX_ATTEMPTS` also blocks the CORRECT PIN once locked. This is intentional (that's what makes it a lockout), but if the user forgets PIN mid-session and hammers, they're locked for 15 min even if they remember. UX-wise a countdown in the UI would help — the 429 message includes the minutes so frontend can show it. Not a blocker.

change_pin does NOT bump lockout counter on wrong old_pin — a persistent attacker with a live token could brute-force old_pin without triggering lockout. But: they already need a valid token (which itself requires a successful unlock). Low severity; noting for defense-in-depth.
